name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Tactical Mesh Suppressor
product_name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Tactical Mesh Suppressor
description:
The Tactical Mesh Suppressor is a portable, directional signal denial system designed to sever mesh network connectivity, encrypted comm channels, and emergency broadcast access within a defined operational envelope. Roughly the size and weight of a hardback book, it deploys as a handheld unit or mounts magnetically to surfaces and vehicles. Its suppression field is not a simple broadband jammer — the Suppressor uses Arcturus's Selective Denial Architecture to target specific protocol layers of GLMZ's civilian and corporate mesh infrastructure while leaving defined frequencies open for operator use, preventing the self-defeating blackout that affects cruder jamming equipment.

The Selective Denial Architecture is the product's defining feature and the basis of its legal classification. By suppressing at the protocol level rather than the frequency level, the Suppressor can deny mesh access, encrypted comms, and automated distress signaling simultaneously without producing the detectable jamming signature that conventional frequency-blocking devices emit. From the outside, affected devices appear to be experiencing routine connectivity degradation — the kind of outage that happens a dozen times a day across GLMZ's aging infrastructure. Only prolonged, precise spectrum analysis can distinguish a Suppressor field from genuine network failure.

Arcturus sells the Suppressor through its law enforcement and corporate security divisions with appropriate licensing frameworks, and the device appears regularly in the inventories of precinct security teams, corporate extraction units, and private protection details. Its presence on the black market is equally routine, and the gap between the licensed and unlicensed versions is primarily one of firmware — the licensed variant has hardcoded duration limits and automatic logging; the black-market variant does not.

specifications.suppression_envelope: Directional cone, 15° to 120° adjustable spread; effective range 40m standard, 180m maximum (reduced fidelity)
specifications.protocols_targeted: GLMZ Civic Mesh v4.1–v6.3, CorpNet Standard B and C, encrypted VoIP over mesh, automated emergency distress broadcast
specifications.licensed_firmware_limits: 90-minute maximum activation, mandatory event logging to Arcturus compliance server
specifications.black_market_firmware: Unlimited duration, logging disabled, suppression envelope expanded by 22%
specifications.detection_resistance: Indistinguishable from network degradation to standard intercept equipment; detectable by military-grade spectrum analysis

tactical_use: The Suppressor is standard equipment for corporate extraction teams conducting personnel recovery in hostile precincts — cutting mesh access prevents targets from calling for support or triggering automated alerts. Security teams use it to create communication dead zones around high-value meetings, ensuring that no attendee can transmit from within the envelope. Criminals use it to blind security infrastructure during operations, producing what appears to be a routine connectivity outage in the affected block. Its directional nature allows experienced operators to suppress specific areas while leaving adjacent zones unaffected — surgically isolating a target without triggering the broader alarm that a full-block blackout might generate.
cultural_context: The Interdict is what people mean when they say a neighborhood 'went dark.' In GLMZ, sudden mesh dropouts are common enough that most residents have learned to recognize the particular quality of a Suppressor-induced outage versus genuine infrastructure failure — the former tends to have cleaner edges, affecting some blocks precisely while leaving adjacent ones unaffected. Street-level awareness of the Suppressor has generated a folk practice of keeping analog fallbacks: physical signal mirrors, chalk marks, runner networks. Among corporate security professionals, carrying a Suppressor is a mark of operational seriousness. Among the people those professionals are deployed against, it is a symbol of the asymmetry that defines life in the lower precincts.
known_users: Syndicate operational crews (black market firmware variant)
story_hooks: A neighborhood has experienced daily mesh outages at the same time each evening for three weeks — someone is running a Suppressor on a schedule, and no one knows why.
The players are mid-operation when the mesh drops. It could be infrastructure failure. It probably isn't.

A licensed Suppressor's compliance logs — which are supposed to transmit automatically to Arcturus's servers — show a 6-hour gap that the device's internal clock doesn't account for. Someone used it off-books, and Arcturus wants to know who.
A contact needs the players to keep a specific area mesh-active during an operation — meaning they need to find and disable a Suppressor that's already in place before the window closes.

Black-market Suppressors with modified firmware are appearing in unprecedented numbers in a particular precinct, suggesting someone is mass-distributing them in preparation for something large enough to require sustained communication blackouts.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, rectangular device resembling a hardcover book or thick tablet. Angular, purposeful industrial design with slightly beveled edges. The form factor suggests both portability and deliberate concealment—it could pass as a technical manual or datapad at a glance. Asymmetrical weight distribution favors one end, suggesting internal heat-sink architecture.
physical_description.dimensions: 24cm × 15cm × 4.5cm (hardback book size); palm-sized when oriented vertically
physical_description.weight_description: 1.1kg — easily handheld, comfortable for sustained operation, requires carrying strap or cargo pocket for extended fieldwork
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite with embedded aluminum heatsink core; rubberized grips on short edges
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal with microscopic texture to reduce reflectivity and fingerprinting; anodized aluminum accent bezel
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey primary, brushed titanium accents on edges and control elements. Amber warning indicators recessed into top surface
physical_description.interface_elements: Top surface: 7.6cm monochrome LCD display (low-power e-ink style), recessed to minimize profile. Physical controls: rotating directional dial (15°–120° spread), power toggle, preset frequency bank selector (4-position), mode indicator lights (green=operator-reserved channels active, amber=suppression active, red=thermal warning). Bottom: reinforced magnetic mounting plate with grip studs. Rear-facing port cluster (covered by rubberized flap): proprietary charging connector, firmware update port, wired operator terminal jack.
distinctive_features: Asymmetrical heat-sink venting along rear spine — visible parallel fins indicating active thermal management
Recessed antenna array on top surface, barely visible unless backlit — suggests protocol-layer sophistication
Magnetic mounting system reinforced with visible steel inserts at corners
Operator-reserved frequency windows displayed as small amber LEDs in a linear array below main display
Subtle Arcturus Defense Solutions etched logo on lower right corner, deliberately understated
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Small 'Arcturus Defense Solutions / Murmuration Systems' text on bottom plate in 4pt font. Regulatory stamps (GLMZ Tier 3+ licensed equipment marking) and serial number printed on rear. Black market variants show filing damage on manufacturer stamps or replaced plates.
physical_description.condition_typical: In active use: display glowing with suppression envelope metrics and affected protocol counts; amber LEDs indicating operator band reserve status. Slight warmth radiating from rear venting during sustained operation. Magnetic mounting leaves minor dust accumulation around edges. Licensed units show wear patterns consistent with vehicle dashboard mounting; black market units often carry signs of field repair or component swaps.
